reasoning: Preserved the failure-driven clause-by-clause verification rule because it addresses unjustified strengthening and is consistent with the existing skill. Also retained the success-driven FPT-versus-XP distinction as a distinct, reusable runtime check not covered by the failure patch. Both edits are appended outside the protected section.

edits.content: When choices share a core claim, treat every added clause as a separate proof obligation, and rank options only after establishing all their clauses. An implication between choices helps compare their strength; it does not establish the stronger choice. In particular, graph isomorphism need not preserve covering actions, a decision algorithm need not construct witnesses, and qualitative existence or regularity does not by itself imply a sharper rate, sign, asymptotic expansion, long-time bound, or quantitative estimate with the same domain for the data. For local estimates, check cutoff and boundary terms and whether larger-set or solution norms are required. For classifications, verify the exact allowed parameter set rather than extrapolating from an analogous structure.

### Track parameter dependence in runtime bounds
For parameterized complexity claims, distinguish a uniform FPT bound, of the form f(k)n^C with C independent of k, from an XP bound such as n^{g(k)}. Polynomial time for each fixed k does not by itself establish FPT if the polynomial's exponent may depend on k. Compare the stated uniform runtime, not just the fixed-parameter consequence.
